Input decisions: S2-FAST, ML-1 and ML-2 in the same situations

  • Each example opens about 1.1 s before your gesture, with the real game as you played it (the same on all three boards; gray line = where David came from). From the moment the gesture began, each board shows what that method does with your actual finger movement: it reads your finger for 250 ms, and, if it turned David, until his next regular step for one more turn (the second half of a one-cell side step or U-turn); then David goes straight until he eats the harp or dies, as the scoring assumes.
  • Only spears from attackers already on screen when the gesture began are simulated (attackers aim at where David is, so later ones would differ).
  • Score: harp +1; a death costs −0.5, less the later it comes (decay length 1 step for wall and tail, 3.7 for spears); a spear from the side costs nothing.
  • Paths: the line shows the whole run (dashed = still to come); rings mark the turns. On the finger panel, the rings mark the finger sample at which each method turned (biggest = S2-FAST, middle = ML-1, smallest = ML-2); gray = finger movement before or after the gesture's input.
  • Keys: space play/pause, ← → one tick, g gesture start, ↑ ↓ previous / next example.
